findings.problem: fs::read_to_string(path).unwrap() — unwrap on I/O Result panics on missing file, permission error, or truncated read
findings.failure_mode: untrusted or missing file path aborts the entire program instead of returning a typed I/O error
findings.fix: return Result<Vec<Record>, std::io::Error> (or a typed domain error) and use ? to propagate the error

findings.problem: parts[1].parse::<u32>().unwrap() — unwrap on ParseIntResult panics on non-numeric content
findings.failure_mode: malformed CSV data (e.g. 'alice,foo') panics instead of returning a typed ParseError
findings.fix: use .parse::<u16>().map_err(|e| ParseError(...)) and propagate via ?; parse directly to u16 to skip the width mismatch

findings.problem: parse::<u32>().unwrap() as u16 — lossy width cast after parse
findings.failure_mode: values > 65535 silently truncate to u16 range; a '100000' string succeeds but corrupts data
findings.fix: parse directly to u16: parts[1].parse::<u16>().map_err(...) — no cast needed, out-of-range is a typed error

findings.problem: split(',').map(...).collect() into Vec<String> to extract two fields — allocates intermediate collection
findings.failure_mode: wastes heap allocation for a fixed two-field parse; also masks the fact that only parts[0] and parts[1] are used
findings.fix: use split_once(',') to get (name, rest), trim name, then parse rest; no Vec allocation

findings.problem: println!("loaded {}", parts[0]) — hidden I/O / side effect inside core parsing logic
findings.failure_mode: pure parsing function has observable side effects, making it untestable in isolation and coupling the core to the console
findings.fix: remove println! entirely; if logging is needed, push it to the imperative shell that calls this function

findings.problem: load_sessions mixes I/O (fs::read_to_string), pure parsing, and console logging in one function
findings.failure_mode: cannot unit-test the parsing logic without mocking the filesystem or suppressing stdout
findings.fix: split into: (1) a pure fn parse_records(lines: impl IntoIterator<Item = &str>) -> Result<Vec<Record>, ParseError>; (2) a shell fn load_sessions(path: &str) -> Result<Vec<Record>, Error> that reads, logs, and calls (1)

findings.problem: Function returns Vec<Record> directly instead of Result — any fallible operation inside must unwrap/panic
findings.failure_mode: design forces unwrap() usage; no way for callers to distinguish success from I/O, parse, or data errors
findings.fix: return Result<Vec<Record>, SessionError> where SessionError is an enum with I/O and Parse variants

findings.problem: parts[0] accessed without bounds check — if line is empty or has no comma, split yields single element
findings.failure_mode: IndexOutOfBounds panic on blank lines or lines without a comma delimiter
findings.fix: use split_once(',') and match the Some((name, rest)) / None arms explicitly

findings.problem: parts[1] accessed without bounds check — same indexing risk as line 16
findings.failure_mode: IndexOutOfBounds panic on lines with a comma but no second field (e.g. 'alice,')
findings.fix: use split_once(',') and extract rest from the Some arm; parse rest directly
